newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-JOYNER-KERSEE TO CONCENTRATE ON TRACK.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOYNER-KERSEE TO CONCENTRATE ON TRACK.

text.p: Jackie Joyner-Kersee is putting away the basketball and putting on her track shoes again.

"I haven't done anything track related since the Olympics, except running up and down the court, so I have to really be realistic and not over do it, "Joyner-Kersee said of the decision to abandon her basketball career to return to the track beginning with the Millrose Games on February 7.

Winner of six Olympic medals in the long jump and heptathlon, Joyner-Kersee is one of 70 former Olympians expected to compete in the 83rd Millrose Games at Madison Square Garden next month according to meet director Howard Schmertz.
Joyner-Kersee is scheduled to run in the 60-meter hurdles against a strong field that will include fellow-American Olympians Tonya Burford-Bailey and Michelle Freeman, Schmertz said.
Last fall Joyner-Kersse joined the Richmond Rage of the fledging first-year women's professional American Basketball League.
"As much as I love playing, I don't like the idea of getting injured," the 34-year-old Joyner-Kersee said of leaving the team midway through the 40-game season.
"If I'm in the hurdles, people will be ready to go (after her," said Joyner-Kersee, the 1995 Millrose hurdles winner. "I have to get my act together."
Joyner-Kersee's last track appearance was bittersweet at the Atlanta Games.

Her bid to win a a third consecutive heptathlon gold medal ended in tears after the first event when an injury to her right hamstring forced her out of the competition. She returned a few days later and managed to win a bronze medal in the long jump.
"All I wanted was to compete on American soil, and with the injury it was tough," said Joyner-Kersee, whose first Olympics was in 1998 at Seoul.

Joyner-Kersee intends on competing in the two other U.S. indoor meets in Fairfax, Virginia and Atlanta and said she is keeping her options open about qualifying for the World Indoor Championships in Paris in March.
"My motives are the same as they have always been, to get out there and compete to the best of my ability," Joyner-Kersee said. "It's not to prove anything."
Joyner-Kersee played only sparingly for the Rage, averaging about 3-5 minutes a games and only a few points and rebounds a game.
However, she was not disappointed with her play after not playing basketball since graduating from UCLA in 1985.
"When I went into, I wasn't looking to go and try to be a superstar," said Joyner-Kersee."I wanted the challenge and I've enjoyed it.
"I'm glad I didn't stay at home and said I could've, would've and should've'."
